description: Exploratory screen of the standard controller's window length under the enforceable processed-block window semantics. The announcement-semantics smoke showed that the historical signal's zero-width EbAnnounced entries shorten the effective window at contended loads (to roughly 10-13 processed blocks), and that a clean 20-processed-block window loses launch-day retained value against it. Announcement entries are not adoptable in the ledger rule: an announcement is a costless, unpunishable producer claim, so counting it would hand producers a free lever on the standard quote. This screen therefore asks whether a shorter processed-block window recovers the historical performance. Arms: the historical announcement-diluted 20-entry window (reference), flat fee (baseline), and processed-block windows of 10, 13, 15, and 20. Everything else is fixed at S=.75/U=.50, D16, half-RB threshold, K10, announcement-time age reset. One hundred paired seeds across the five headline loads plus the 0.1 tx/slot trickle. This is a screen: any selected length needs confirmation on disjoint seeds before adoption.
